signs.default_1_title: They keep circling after they have lain down.
signs.default_1_text: A few turns before settling is just what dogs do. Turning, resettling, then shifting again ten minutes later usually means no position on that bed takes the weight off.
signs.default_2_title: They have started choosing the floor.
signs.default_2_text: Once foam has bottomed out, hard tiles genuinely are the firmer, flatter option. A dog picking the kitchen floor over their own bed has done the comparison and reached a conclusion.
signs.default_3_title: There's a dip that doesn't spring back.
signs.default_3_text: Press a flat hand into the middle where they lie. If you can feel the floor through it, so can their hips and elbows.

faq.size_q: How do I know which size to get?
faq.size_a_html: Measure nose to base of tail while they are lying down, then add 15–20cm. Where a dog falls between two sizes, go up: sprawlers need the length more than you would think. Every product page has a size guide built from that bed's own measurements, with breed examples.
faq.foam_q: What's inside the orthopaedic beds? Isn't firmer better?
faq.foam_a_html:
Foam, rather than loose filling. Firmness is only how a bed feels on day one; what matters is whether it still holds them up a few winters on. Loose fibre shifts and packs down under a dog's weight, and foam keeps its shape far longer.

Many of the orthopaedic beds pair memory foam, which contours to hip and shoulder, with a profiled egg-crate layer underneath that spreads their weight. The fibre-filled nest beds are built for softness instead. Each product page says exactly what's inside that bed.
faq.wash_a_html:
On most of the range, yes: properly, not just spot-clean. Most covers zip off and wash, following the care label sewn into each one, and selected beds have a waterproof inner liner that keeps wet coats, muddy paws and accidents away from the foam. Each product page says whether that bed has one.

One exception worth knowing before you buy: waterproof-fabric beds are wiped clean rather than washed with detergent, because detergent strips the coating off the fabric. Every product page says which applies.
faq.delivery_cutoff_html: Orders go out on working days, tracked from the moment they leave us. Order by {{ cutoff }} on a dispatch day and it goes the same day; most then arrive within {{ days }} working days. Tracking comes by email as soon as it's on its way.
faq.delivery_cutoff_next_html: Orders go out on working days, tracked from the moment they leave us. Order by {{ cutoff }} on a dispatch day and it goes the same day; most then arrive the next working day. Tracking comes by email as soon as it's on its way.
faq.delivery_plain_html: Orders go out on working days and are tracked from the moment they leave us. You'll see the delivery options and their cost at checkout before you pay, and tracking comes by email as soon as it's on its way.
faq.delivery_free_html: Standard delivery is free on UK orders over {{ amount }}. Any delivery charge, including Express if you choose it, is shown at checkout before you pay.
faq.trial_q: What if my dog just won't use it?
faq.trial_a_html: Then it comes back. Let your dog sleep on it for up to {{ nights }} nights. {{ terms }} Just tell us inside that window. It doesn't need to be unused: send it back slept-on, hair and all. Full terms are in our returns policy.
faq.trial_a_nolink_html: Then it comes back. Let your dog sleep on it for up to {{ nights }} nights. {{ terms }} Just tell us inside that window. It doesn't need to be unused: send it back slept-on, hair and all.
faq.guarantee_q: What does the {{ years }}-year guarantee cover?
faq.guarantee_a_html: The foam. Our orthopaedic memory foam beds carry a {{ years }}-year guarantee on the core, marked on each bed's page: if the foam loses its structure under normal use in that time, which is the failure that ends most dog beds, we'll replace it. Covers, zips and liners are wearing parts and sit outside it, and beds whose page doesn't mention the guarantee, such as the fibre-filled nest beds, aren't covered. Full terms are in our returns policy.
faq.guarantee_a_nolink_html: The foam. Our orthopaedic memory foam beds carry a {{ years }}-year guarantee on the core, marked on each bed's page: if the foam loses its structure under normal use in that time, which is the failure that ends most dog beds, we'll replace it. Covers, zips and liners are wearing parts and sit outside it, and beds whose page doesn't mention the guarantee, such as the fibre-filled nest beds, aren't covered.
faq.arthritis_q: Will it help a dog with arthritis or stiff hips?
faq.arthritis_a_html: A supportive bed spreads their weight so pressure isn't concentrated on hips, elbows and shoulders, which is what makes lying down and getting back up harder for a dog with joint wear. But a bed is not a treatment and it won't replace veterinary care, so please keep talking to your vet. What it can change is the surface they spend twelve to fourteen hours a day on.
